import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'is_takeaway' to a more descriptive categorical variable
df['order_type'] = df['is_takeaway'].map({0: 'Dine-in', 1: 'Takeaway'})

# Aggregate total sales by product and order type
# This will show which products are most popular and how their sales split between dine-in and takeaway
sales_by_product_and_type = df.groupby(['product', 'order_type'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.barplot(
    data=sales_by_product_and_type,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='order_type',
    palette='viridis',
    errorbar=None  # No error bars needed for aggregated sums
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Order Type', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if product names are long
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Order Type', title_fontsize='11', fontsize='10', loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

# Improve layout and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset

# Set a style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the bar plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
sns.barplot(
    data=sales_by_product_and_type,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='order_type',
    palette='viridis',
    errorbar=None  # No error bars needed for aggregated sums
)

# Add title and labels

plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
